newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Four-nation EFTA initials Morocco trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Four-nation EFTA initials Morocco trade pact.

text.p: The four-nation European Free Trade Association (EFTA) on Tuesday initialled a free trade pact with Morocco which is to be formally signed at a ministerial meeting in Geneva next week.

A statement from EFTA -- which links Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein -- said the agreement marked a major breakthrough for the grouping in the Mediterranean region and others were likey to follow.

The accord, initialled in Oslo, provides for free trade in industrial products, processed agricultural goods, fish and other marine products. Trade in farm produce is being negotiated bilaterally between the four countries and Morocco.
The Geneva-headquartered EFTA said its members would eliminate all duties and restrictions on products covered as soon as it went into force -- expected to be by January 1 next year at the latest.

Morocco would abolish its own duties on EFTA imports over a transition period of 12 years, and would be allowed to introduce temporary measures to protect infant industries and sectors of its own economy undergoing restructuring or in difficulty.

The pact follows similar deals EFTA has signed with Turkey and Israel at the other end of the Mediterranean. Talks on a similar deal are under way with Tunisia and negotiations with Cyprus and Malta are to begin later in the year.

The grouping, which once included six of the present members of the 15-state European Union, also has free trade pacts with most ex-communist states of eastern Europe and is negotiating with ex-Soviet Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia.
Despite its relatively small size, EFTA has a trade volume of about one sixth of that of the EU and Swiss and Norwegian companies play important roles in the international economy.

EFTA said the accord with Morocco, and the others in the pipeline would ensure that companies based in its four member states would become full participants in the Euro-Mediterranean free trade zone the EU aims to complete by the year 2010.

Three members of EFTA -- Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein -- are linked to the EU in the European Economic Area (EEA). But Switzerland voted against joining the EEA in a 1992 referendum and is negotiating bilateral accords with Brussels.
